question: Which metal ion released from tannery industry causes acute water pollution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cr.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chromium**:-

 
 
• **The metal ion released from tannery industry that causes acute water pollution is chromium (Cr).**
 
• Chromium is a heavy metal and a toxic pollutant that can cause severe health problems such as cancer, liver and kidney damage, and respiratory issues.
 
• **Tannery industry uses chromium in the form of chromium salts as a tanning agent to process animal hides and skins into leather.**
 
• The wastewater generated from tannery industry contains high levels of chromium, which is discharged into water bodies without proper treatment, leading to acute water pollution. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Magnesium (Mg):-**

 
 
• ​__It is an essential mineral that is commonly found in water and soil. It is not considered a toxic pollutant and does not cause acute water pollution.
 
 
 
• **Arsenic**:-
 
 
• As is a toxic metalloid that can cause serious health problems such as skin lesions, cancer, and cardiovascular disease. It is commonly found in groundwater in some regions, but it is not directly related to tannery industry pollution.
 
 
 
• **Zinc:-**
 
 
• Zn is a trace element that is essential for human health and is commonly found in water and soil. It is not considered a toxic pollutant and does not cause acute water pollution.
